text:
jess_prod: Hey team — customers hitting a ton of 429s when calling rwd-3-extended with long contexts since yesterday. They send ~6 reqs/sec each with ~60k tokens in the prompt. Errors look like `HTTP 429` with body `rate_limit_exceeded`. Any quick triage tips?

sam_support: Ugh. Can you paste a sample curl + response headers (if available)? Also which API key / org, and is this hosted or Dedicated?

jess_prod: Hosted. Example curl:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"rwd-3-extended","input":"<64k prompt...>","max_tokens":512}'
```
Response headers:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-model-rpm: 300
x-rate-limit-model-tpm: 18000
x-rate-limit-concurrency: 8
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 30
```
Body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"model per-minute quota exceeded"}`

maria_infra: Thanks. Those headers are helpful — looks like model-level RPM/TPM and concurrency are blocking. Note: for long-context variants we apply effective throttles because each request consumes many token-units toward TPM. 60k prompt + 512 output ~= 60512 tokens per request. At 6 reqs/sec that's ~360 reqs/min * 60k tokens ~= 21.6M tokens/min which exceeds model TPM (18k??) — that header `x-rate-limit-model-tpm` seems low but it's per-account-per-model accounting.

tyler_sre: Quick correction: `x-rate-limit-model-tpm: 18000` is probably being reported in token *thousands* for readability in our infra (we've had confusion before). Confirmed mapping: header value is actual token budget per minute. So 18k tokens/min. With 60k tokens per request, 1 request already > TPM so it will always 429.

jess_prod: Oh damn. So it's not concurrency peaking, it's token-cost per request exceeding the minute window. Is that documented somewhere? Our customer assumed TPM only counted generated tokens.

sam_support: We should explain: TPM counts total tokens processed (prompt + completion) and is enforced per-model per-org. For extended context models we also have additional throttles to protect multi-tenant GPUs; extremely large single-request token counts can trigger immediate 429s.

maria_infra: Repro steps for our infra team if you want us to simulate: 1) Use a test key 2) Send single request with ~64k prompt to rwd-3-extended 3) Observe immediate 429 + `retry-after: 30` 4) Try same with smaller prompt (<= 4k) to see success.

jess_prod: I included repro curl above. Should we escalate to product to increase TPM for that org?

lex_billing: Billing note: if TPM increase requested we need usage pattern + estimated monthly token ingestion. Our quota increases for hosted plans require committed usage or dedicated capacity. For short term we can issue a temporary bump but need justification.

sam_support: Suggested customer-facing troubleshooting steps to send to the user: 1) Reduce prompt size or stream context in chunks and summarize before sending. 2) Use model variant `rwd-3-extended-lite` (lower context but higher per-minute throughput) for high-QPS small-context workloads. 3) Request Dedicated / Reserved capacity if they need sustained large-context throughput. 4) Consider client-side batching or pacing to stay within RPM/TPM.

jess_prod: Also saw some `x-rate-limit-concurrency: 8`. Their app does ~20 parallel workers. Could that still matter?

maria_infra: Yes — concurrency limits cap simultaneous model sessions. If they open 20 streams and each is large, you'll hit concurrency + TPM combined. Concurrency is enforced per API key per model variant. For streaming endpoints there is an additional slot hold during open stream which counts toward concurrency.

tyler_sre: Logging snippet from our side when I repro'd:```
[2025-04-11T18:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 model=rwd-3-extended org=org-789 tokens_in=60450 tokens_out=512 tokens_total=60962 tpm_quota=18000 result=throttle token_over=42962
```
That shows single request consumed > tpm_quota and hit throttle path.

jess_prod: Good to have that. Customer asked if there are any headers they can watch client-side to pre-empt 429s?

sam_support: Yes — we send: `x-rate-limit-model-rpm`, `x-rate-limit-model-tpm`, `x-rate-limit-concurrency`, `x-rate-limit-remaining` and `retry-after`. They can poll remaining or respect `retry-after`. Also implement exponential backoff on 429s.

jess_prod: They want a short reproducible note to give devs. I'll paste this: "Large single requests against extended-context models count full prompt+completion toward TPM. If your prompt size > model TPM, you'll get immediate 429s. To avoid: chunk + summarize, choose a higher-throughput variant, or request Dedicated capacity." Good?

maria_infra: Perfect. Add a note to recommend checking `x-rate-limit-model-tpm` before sending huge payloads. If `prompt_tokens > tpm` then error is guaranteed.

lex_billing: For customers pushing >100M tokens/month we recommend dedicated reservations. I'll follow up with pricing and a temporary quota bump offer (30d trial) if they can share expected monthly tokens.

rwd-monitor-bot: Incident alert: spike detected 2025-04-11T17:55:00Z -> 2025-04-11T19:05:00Z, 429 rate increased by 420% for rwd-3-extended in us-west1.

sam_support: Action items: @maria_infra will add a short KB blurb clarifying TPM semantics for extended models; @lex_billing will propose temporary TPM bump + next-steps for Dedicated; @jess_prod please share customer logs + org id.

maria_infra: I'll also talk to runtime team about making the token-mapping in headers less ambiguous (tyler pointed out earlier mismatch).

jess_prod: Sent org id in DM and included sample logs. Thanks all — I’ll relay troubleshooting and mitigation steps to the customer. :thumbsup:

tyler_sre: One more tip for them: if they need to send long docs, precompute embeddings and only send relevant chunks during generation. That cuts prompt size massively and keeps you under TPM.

jess_prod: Closing loop — customer implemented chunk+summary flow and errors dropped to near zero. They asked for a docs link we can share later.

sam_support: I'll draft a KB and link it in this thread when ready.```
